title: Crisis Management and Resolution
summary: A ten-module programme preparing supervisors for firm and system-wide stress, from early intervention and recovery and resolution planning to crisis communication and a live simulation.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors to act early and decisively when firms or markets come under stress: recognising warning signs, intervening, assessing recovery and resolution plans, managing contagion and communicating under pressure.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To build the capability authorities need for the moments that matter most but occur least, from early intervention through recovery and resolution to system-wide stress. Participants leave able to recognise distress early, escalate with confidence, judge the credibility of recovery and resolution plans, and make and communicate decisions under time pressure.
sections.What It Covers: The authority's role in a crisis, early warning indicators, the intervention ladder, recovery planning, resolution planning and resolvability, resolution tools and orderly failure, systemic risk and contagion, macroprudential tools, crisis communication and coordination, and a firm-distress simulation.
Intended Audience: Supervisors and risk specialists responsible for firms that may come under stress
Resolution, financial stability and macroprudential staff
Senior managers and executives who would lead or take decisions in the authority's crisis response
Learning Objectives: Explain the roles of supervisors, resolution authorities and other bodies in a financial crisis
Identify early warning signs and apply a structured intervention ladder
Assess the credibility of recovery plans and the resolvability of firms
Evaluate systemic risk, contagion channels and the macroprudential tools to address them
Communicate and coordinate effectively with the public, industry, government and other authorities
Make and evaluate supervisory decisions under time pressure in a simulated crisis
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short input with case studies and exercises, ending in a live crisis simulation and debrief, and can be selected or tailored to the authority's sectors and resolution framework.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervision, financial stability or risk work is helpful. No prior crisis or resolution experience is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
Basel Committee, Guidelines for Identifying and Dealing with Weak Banks (2015)
IADI, Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems

modules.title: Financial Crises and the Authority's Role
modules.summary: How firms and markets fail, the roles of the supervisor, resolution authority, central bank and protection schemes, and how an authority organises itself to take crisis decisions.
objectives: Explain the common paths from stress to failure
Describe the roles of the authorities involved in a crisis
Assess the authority's own crisis governance and readiness
syllabus: Anatomy of firm failure: solvency, liquidity, conduct and operational triggers
Supervisors, resolution authorities, central banks and protection schemes
FSB Key Attributes and IADI principles
Crisis governance: decision rights, playbooks and escalation within the authority

modules.title: Early Warning Indicators and Signs of Distress
modules.summary: The quantitative and behavioural signals that typically precede firm distress, and how supervisors build them into monitoring so problems are spotted while there is still time to act.
objectives: Identify common early warning indicators across risk types
Distinguish behavioural from quantitative warning signs
Assess whether monitoring arrangements would detect distress in time
syllabus: Capital, liquidity, earnings and funding indicators
Behavioural signals: management turnover, evasiveness and delayed reporting
Market signals, complaints and whistleblowing
Early warning dashboards and their limits

modules.title: The Intervention Ladder: Escalation and Early Action
modules.summary: How a structured intervention ladder makes escalation consistent and defensible, how to set decision thresholds, and the options available at each rung before problems become crises.
objectives: Explain the intervention ladder from monitoring to formal action
Apply decision thresholds while balancing false alarms against late action
Formulate an early intervention response for a firm in difficulty
syllabus: Why early intervention is more effective and less costly
Thresholds, triggers and documenting escalation decisions
Options at each rung: enhanced monitoring to restrictions and removals
Case study: a firm showing early signs of distress

modules.title: Recovery Planning: Assessing Credibility
modules.summary: How to assess whether a firm's recovery plan would genuinely restore viability under severe stress, and the common weaknesses supervisors should challenge.
objectives: Explain the purpose and content of a recovery plan
Assess recovery indicators, options and scenarios for credibility
Challenge unrealistic assumptions and untested options
syllabus: Recovery plans: governance, indicators, options and communication
Severe but plausible scenarios and the capacity of recovery options
Common weaknesses: optimistic timing, value and executability
Exercise: assessing a sample recovery plan

modules.title: Resolution Planning and Resolvability
modules.summary: The distinction between firm-led recovery and authority-led resolution, the supervisor's role in resolution planning, and how to identify and remove barriers to resolvability in advance.
objectives: Distinguish recovery planning from resolution planning
Describe the supervisor's contribution to resolution planning
Evaluate resolvability barriers in structure, data and continuity of services
syllabus: Preferred resolution strategies and the role of the resolution authority
Barriers: legal structure, intra-group dependencies, data and systems
Operational continuity and critical shared services
Case study: a firm with significant resolvability barriers

modules.title: Resolution Tools and Orderly Failure
modules.summary: The tools available to resolve or wind down a failing firm, how they apply across banks, insurers, investment firms and other sectors, and how customers and critical functions are protected.
objectives: Explain the main resolution and wind-down tools and when each is used
Assess how customer assets, deposits and policyholders are protected
Evaluate the practical steps in executing a resolution or orderly wind-down
syllabus: Transfer, bridge institution, bail-in and run-off
Insolvency, special administration and solvent wind-down
Deposit guarantee, investor and policyholder protection and client assets
Resolution weekend: valuation, sequencing and decision-making

modules.title: Systemic Risk and Contagion
modules.summary: What distinguishes systemic from firm-specific risk, how stress spreads between firms and markets, and how authorities identify interconnectedness before it crystallises.
objectives: Explain the drivers of systemic risk, including beyond the banking sector
Describe contagion channels between firms and markets
Identify systemic risk indicators and the data needed to monitor them
syllabus: Interconnectedness, size and substitutability
Contagion: direct exposures, fire sales and confidence effects
Non-bank financial intermediation and cross-border spillovers
Exercise: mapping contagion channels in an interconnected market

modules.title: Macroprudential Tools and System-Wide Monitoring
modules.summary: How authorities monitor the build-up of system-wide vulnerabilities and choose among macroprudential tools, matching each tool to the risk it is designed to address.
objectives: Design a systemic risk dashboard drawing on firm and market data
Assess the main macroprudential tools and their trade-offs
Match tools to specific systemic risk drivers and decide when to deploy them
syllabus: Systemic risk dashboards and system-wide stress testing
Countercyclical and systemic capital buffers
Sectoral capital requirements and borrower-based measures
Case study: an emerging systemic risk and the policy response

modules.title: Crisis Communication and Coordination
modules.summary: How to communicate clearly and quickly with the public, industry and government during a crisis, balance transparency against stability, and coordinate messages and actions across authorities.
objectives: Explain how crisis communication differs from routine communication
Draft clear public statements under time pressure
Coordinate messages and actions across domestic and cross-border authorities
syllabus: Transparency versus financial stability; risks of premature disclosure
Statements, spokespeople and differentiated stakeholder messaging
Crisis management groups and cross-border cooperation agreements
Exercise: drafting a statement against the clock

modules.title: Crisis Simulation: Firm-Specific Distress
modules.summary: A live simulation in which teams respond to an unfolding firm-distress scenario, making supervisory decisions, escalating and coordinating across functions under time pressure, followed by a structured debrief.
objectives: Apply decision-making frameworks under time pressure and incomplete information
Coordinate a response across supervision, legal, resolution and communications
Evaluate decisions made and identify lessons for crisis preparedness
syllabus: Scenario briefing, roles and initial rapid assessment
Escalation, coordination and stakeholder management as the scenario evolves
Facilitator-led debrief comparing team decisions
Workshop: the authority's crisis preparedness action plan

related.title: Authorisation and Licensing: The Regulatory Gateway
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving authorisation staff a structured, defensible methodology for assessing applications, key individuals, owners and changes at the regulatory gateway.

related.title: Conducting Regulatory Investigations: From Referral to Outcome
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme taking enforcement staff through a regulatory investigation, from referral and powers to compelled interviews, findings and outcome.

related.title: Enforcement and Sanctions
related.summary: A ten-module programme taking enforcement and supervisory staff through the full life of an enforcement case, from triage and evidence to sanctions, settlement and cooperation.

related.title: Fit and Proper Assessments: Approving Owners, Directors and Key Function Holders
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on assessing owners, controllers, directors and key function holders, from evidence gathering and interviews to defensible decisions.

related.title: Policy-Making and Rule-Making
related.summary: An eight-module programme covering the full policy cycle, from problem definition and cost-benefit analysis to drafting, standards implementation and post-implementation review.

related.title: Assessing Board Effectiveness
related.summary: An eight-module programme showing supervisors how to assess how a board really works, from papers and decisions to culture and challenge, culminating in case-study interviews.
